tests.reason: Untestable (no way): Terminal.app 2.15 on macOS exposes no observable in this version and setup that could carry an OSC 133 B prompt-end boundary inside the prompt line. Exercised on Terminal.app 2.15 (bundle CDHash arm64 113489a0, x86_64 df446fa4) on macOS 26.6.2 build 25G83 at shipped settings, owned Mac, 2026-11-18: screen text through the scripting dictionary's contents and history; window pixels with View > Show Marks; Terminal's own line marks and Edit > Navigate > Select to Previous Mark, whose control (a keyboard prompt auto-mark) stops the selection, while after the emitted sequences the selection ran to the first line, so none left a navigable mark (this says nothing about hidden protocol state) - and the mark store is set by keyboard prompt marking with no protocol-created control, so it cannot decide this row; the accessibility tree of the window, walked completely (elements_complete true, 11 elements, every attribute, parameterized attribute and action listed), whose text area offers only AXValue screen text, selection ranges, line geometry and AXStringForRange plain text, with no attributed-string, style or mark attribute, and whose window AXDocument carries the working directory as a full file URL that follows OSC 7; the scripting dictionary (Terminal.sdef SHA256 efc515ec), whose tab properties are contents, history, processes, busy, tty and titles; and the window title and proxy icon, which show the AXDocument folder name. No reachable read shows this sequence's effect; this records the observation surface, not whether Terminal.app parses the sequence.
